tasks.short: Answer media inquiries and arrange the right spokesperson.

steps.what: Read the media inquiry in the {EMAIL} and record its deadline.
Find relevant facts, previous responses and approved releases in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Inquiry text and permission-filtered documents retrieved from the {DOCS}.
loop.output: Relevant passages with source links, approval dates and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require a supporting passage for each fact; flag expired approvals and conflicting sources.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt across at most 20 passages; unresolved questions return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search retrieves documents, but varied questions require reading passages to identify relevant answers.

steps.what: Choose the response approach and spokesperson with the relevant subject matter expert.
Draft a written response and spokesperson briefing in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Response plan, source pack and approved response templates.
loop.output: Response draft and briefing with sentence-level factual references.
loop.check: Check names, numbers and quotations against sources; flag unsupported claims and unanswered questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence or sensitive unresolved questions require manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover acknowledgements, but substantive answers require adapting free text to the question.

steps.what: Review factual accuracy, disclosure limits and the proposed response.
Send the approved response and arrange any interview through the {EMAIL}.
Answer follow-up questions or conduct the interview with the journalist.
Update the media inquiry register and assign outstanding follow-ups in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Configure an inquiry queue in the {WORKFLOW}, connected to the {EMAIL}, {CALENDAR} and permission-filtered {DOCS}. Bounded extraction and drafting produce sourced response packs; approval binds the exact response, recipient and release time before sending. The queue records correspondence automatically, while people choose spokespersons, handle conversations and confirm follow-ups.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved facts were scattered, source approval dates were unclear, and response handling depended on personal mailbox habits.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing queues and scheduling controls handle administration; small extraction and drafting loops can work over a restricted source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Embargoes, hostile questions, conflicting facts and spokesperson availability require judgement. Journalist contact data and confidential briefings require GDPR-compliant processing.
tasks.human_edge: Read the journalist's intent, judge when silence would mislead, and maintain trust during difficult exchanges.

ambition.what: Source-linked briefing packs for specialist journalists.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching and chasing to preparing spokespersons and resolving sensitive inquiries. Formal authority to speak for the organisation does not automatically change.

reach.learn: Escalation thresholds, disclosure limits and how to brief an accountable decision maker.

evidence.claim: Archive question answering is being tested; this supports retrieval assistance, not unattended media responses.
A professional-writing experiment included press releases and emails and found productivity gains.
Inquiry routing, version-bound approval and correspondence logging can use configured workflows.

assumptions: Shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates for a mid-size European company.
The queue captures messages automatically; a person confirms deadlines and sensitive classifications.
The sending gate reuses the recorded response approval; edits invalidate that approval.
Access estimates include privacy review and employee consultation where national rules require it; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Which spokespersons can address which subjects?
Where are approved facts, embargoes and disclosure limits recorded?
Can the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR} support shared access and logged sending?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed workflow?
research_questions: How reliably does retrieval distinguish superseded responses from currently approved facts?
Which inquiry categories need specialist legal or financial review?
new_work: Maintain the source approval dates and spokesperson roster.
Review unsupported answers, deadline ambiguities and sensitive inquiries.
Confirm conversation follow-ups and remove contact data under the retention policy.
Maintain connectors, permissions and response templates.

tasks.short: Plan communication programmes that build credible public and stakeholder perceptions.

steps.what: Collect objectives, accomplishments, research and previous results from the {DOCS} and {BI}.
Validate proposed accomplishments and environmental claims against supporting records.
Discuss audience concerns, organisational priorities and stakeholder expectations in a planning workshop.
Choose audiences, communication objectives, narrative and programme approach in the {DOCS}.
Write the programme plan, messages, milestones, responsibilities and measurement approach in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Human-chosen strategy, validated evidence, constraints and a programme-plan template.
loop.output: Draft plan with sourced messages, activities, owners, milestones and proposed measures.
loop.check: Validate required fields and dates deterministically; review message credibility and whether measures match objectives.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted revisions; unresolved strategic choices return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates structure the plan, but translating a chosen narrative into audience-specific messages requires writing.

steps.what: Approve the programme plan, budget and delegated delivery responsibilities.
Brief delivery teams and agree dependencies and handoffs.
Combine delivery updates and perception measures in the {SPREADSHEET} for the next review.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles a permission-filtered evidence pack from the {DOCS} and {BI}; experts validate the claims before use. A bounded drafting loop turns the human-chosen strategy into a structured plan, then approval in the {WORKFLOW} releases delivery tasks to the {PROJECT}. A {BI} view assembles programme results for review, with separate approval for later public communications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence collection, version reconciliation and plan formatting were costly, while strategy depended on stakeholder knowledge that templates could not supply.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable schemas and connectors reduce assembly work; bounded drafting can turn an explicit strategy into a reviewable plan.
tasks.still_hard: Credible environmental claims, competing stakeholder interests and attribution of perception changes remain difficult. Faster writing does not establish that a programme will improve trust.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a defensible narrative, challenge weak claims and negotiate commitments that the organisation can actually deliver.

ambition.what: Monthly reassessment of programme messages against new audience concerns.

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to stakeholder listening, programme choices and testing assumptions. The specialist can propose smaller message experiments more often; budget and public commitments retain their existing approval rights.

reach.learn: Evidence boundaries, measurement periods and how to communicate uncertainty.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.learn: Sampling, question wording and the limits of attributing changes to communication.

evidence.claim: A professional-writing experiment supports assistance with reports and press releases; it does not demonstrate better communication strategy.
Coosto offers conversation and news-topic monitoring, providing a possible input to programme review.
Evidence-pack assembly, structured plans and delivery dashboards can use deterministic integrations.

assumptions: Shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
The programme plan is an internal artefact; approving it does not approve every later public claim.
Source metrics are accessible through permitted exports or interfaces.
Access estimates include GDPR review and employee consultation where national rules require it; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Which teams can validate financial, operational and environmental claims?
Are perception measures available beyond reach and engagement counts?
Who approves budgets and public commitments?
Which source-access and national employee-consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which existing measures distinguish audience understanding from exposure?
Can reviewers trace every proposed message to evidence and its limitations?
How much plan preparation remains after stakeholder decisions are explicit?
new_work: Maintain evidence owners, metric definitions and claim expiry dates.
Review generated messages for overstatement and missing qualifications.
Investigate data gaps and distinguish association from programme impact.
Maintain plan templates, connectors and delivery mappings.

tasks.short: Prepare, approve and publish website and social content.

steps.what: Receive the approved brief, copy and assets through the {EMAIL}.
Adapt copy, captions and accessibility descriptions for each channel in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved source copy, supplied assets, channel limits and accessibility guidance.
loop.output: Channel variants, captions and proposed image descriptions.
loop.check: Check length, required links, terms and factual references; a person checks image descriptions and meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per channel across at most five channels; uncertain descriptions return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Formatting rules cannot reliably shorten free text or describe images while preserving meaning; unchanged copy bypasses the loop.

steps.what: Apply templates and attach assets in the {CMS} and {SOCIAL}.
Review previews, claims, asset rights, accessibility, destinations and release timing.
Publish or schedule the approved website content in the {CMS}.
Publish or schedule the approved social posts in the {SOCIAL}.
Check live pages, posts and links against the approved previews.
Copy publication links and dates into the content register in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Configure content intake, templates, previews and scheduling across the {WORKFLOW}, {CMS} and {SOCIAL}; use a bounded drafting loop only for channel adaptation. Approval binds the content version, assets, destinations and release time, and any edit invalidates it before publication. A deterministic job checks published text and links, flags rendering checks for people, and uses publication receipts as the content register.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channel preparation involved repeated copying, separate approval messages and inconsistent publication records. Existing publishing features were often only partly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration handles most staging and scheduling; inexpensive custom checks connect publication receipts, approvals and link validation.
tasks.still_hard: Channel permissions, interface limits, image rights and visual rendering vary. Context-sensitive wording and accessibility descriptions still need review.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a technically correct post is appropriate for the audience and current events.

ambition.what: Accessible channel-ready publication packs for small internal teams.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from uploading and copying links to reviewing content and helping internal teams communicate. Existing publishing authority remains; additional channel rights require explicit delegation.

reach.task: Run a shared editorial calendar and resolve competing publication priorities.
reach.learn: Editorial selection, audience fit and publication sequencing.
Responsive layout, semantic structure and practical accessibility testing.

evidence.claim: Coosto provides social-post scheduling, supporting configuration before custom publishing code.
Acrolinx provides repeatable house-style checks and quality gates.
Version-bound approvals, publication receipts and link checks can be implemented deterministically.

assumptions: Shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates; today's screen use exceeds the supplied prior for this publishing task.
The {CMS} and {SOCIAL} support drafts, scheduling and appropriate publication access.
The publication gates reuse the preview approval rather than requiring repeated approval.
GDPR and EU AI Act transparency duties are assessed for the content; human review is recorded where relevant.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Which publication interfaces and scheduling features are available?
Who may approve each channel, claim category and release time?
Are asset licences and consent records available with the asset pack?
Does the content register contain obligations beyond links and publication dates?
research_questions: Can every target channel preserve approved formatting, links and accessibility descriptions?
Which live-content checks can be automated reliably, and which require visual inspection?
Can publication approval be invalidated immediately when content changes?
new_work: Review channel variants, image descriptions and publication exceptions.
Maintain templates, channel limits and publishing credentials.
Check rights, consent and applicable disclosure requirements.
Handle failed, partial or mistimed publication and approve corrections.

tasks.short: Write accurate, newsworthy press releases and media communications.

steps.what: Discuss the announcement, intended audience and constraints with the commissioning stakeholder.
Collect factual records, authorised quotations and background material from the {DOCS}.
Choose the news angle, key message and supporting facts.
Write the headline, lead, body, quotations and background section in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Chosen release angle, brief, source pack, authorised quotations and house style.
loop.output: Release draft with claim references and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Require references for factual assertions; match quotations exactly; check names, numbers and mandatory sections.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions; unsupported claims remain marked and unresolved gaps require manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but coherent prose from varied announcements requires bounded writing.

steps.what: Edit the release for spelling, house style, clarity and source consistency.
Validate claims, quotations and qualifications against the underlying facts.
Approve the final release, recipients, embargo and release time.
Send the approved release to the agreed media list through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A structured brief and a source pack in the {DOCS} feed a bounded release generator, with configured terminology, quotation and style checks. Experts validate claims and the manager approves the exact release, recipients and timing in the {WORKFLOW}; the {EMAIL} then sends that approved version. The approved release becomes reusable source material for media responses and publication through the {CMS} and {SOCIAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates helped structure releases but could not reliably turn varied source material into prose. Fact gathering and approval were fragmented across conversations and document versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can create a first version from a controlled source pack, while deterministic checks enforce quotations, terminology and required fields.
tasks.still_hard: Newsworthiness, persuasive but defensible framing, missing evidence and quotation approval remain human work. Embargoed information needs controlled processing, and GDPR and applicable EU AI Act transparency duties still apply.
tasks.human_edge: Find the consequential story, resist unsupported promotion and secure wording that both experts and journalists can trust.

ambition.what: Source-linked press kits for technical announcements.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward interviewing experts, finding stronger angles and improving evidence. Draft preparation expands, while final release and disclosure authority remain with the existing approvers.

reach.task: Translate technical evidence into an accurate press-kit explainer.
reach.learn: Audience modelling, technical verification and explanation without losing essential qualifications.

reach.task: Assess news value and strengthen the release structure.
reach.learn: Headline judgement, evidence ordering and substantive editing.

evidence.claim: The writing experiment included press releases and found faster completion and higher assessed quality; it does not establish savings for this complete workflow.
LanguageTool checks spelling, grammar, punctuation and style.
Acrolinx supports repeatable house-style scoring and quality gates.
A documented invented-quotation incident supports retaining quotation provenance and human factual checks.

assumptions: Shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not extrapolations from the writing experiment.
Drafting uses approved processing arrangements for confidential and personal data.
Configured checks flag style and exact-value discrepancies; they do not certify the truth of prose.
The sending gate reuses final distribution approval, and any substantive edit requires renewed validation.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Who can authorise quotations and validate each claim category?
Where are source records, embargoes and approval histories stored?
Which announcements require additional legal or financial review?
Can approved release versions be locked through distribution?
research_questions: Does a representative release sample retain qualifications and quotation accuracy after drafting?
Which release types fit templates and which need substantial original writing?
Can reviewers verify claims faster using the generated references?
new_work: Review draft framing, factual references and unsupported passages.
Maintain house style, source-pack requirements and quotation permissions.
Handle contradictory evidence and approval changes.
Maintain distribution controls and assess applicable AI disclosure requirements.

role.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling documents, copying content and maintaining registers, and more time interviewing experts, listening to audiences and judging credible messages. Drafting capacity increases; authority over budgets, sensitive disclosures and public commitments changes only through explicit delegation.
reach: Public Relations Managers: develop escalation options and crisis briefings.
Sustainability Specialists: substantiate environmental claims and communicate evidence limits.
Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists: design credible perception measures.
Editors and Technical Writers: strengthen news judgement and evidence-led explanations.
skills_to_grow: Source provenance, quotation verification and claim substantiation.
Structured briefs, reusable templates and deterministic workflow design.
Review of bounded model outputs and handling unsupported claims.
Audience research, programme measurement and attribution limits.
Accessible publishing and channel quality checks.
GDPR, EU AI Act transparency and applicable national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Run an evidence-led communications desk that produces source-linked press kits, accessible channel packs and journalist briefings, while using monthly audience reviews to improve programme choices.
